prompt: GNU diff expand-tabs encoding error column width treatment
answer:
GNU `diff` treats each byte of an encoding error as occupying **one display column**. This is a practical guess, since there is no standard column width for encoding errors; other programs may display such bytes using different widths. [Paul Eggert’s explanation](https://public-inbox.org/bug-gnulib/9946e92b-daca-7c7c-bf8d-ff95897774f3@cs.ucla.edu/)

For tabs:

- `-t` / `--expand-tabs` expands tabs to spaces in the output.
- The default tab stop is every **8 print columns**; `--tabsize=NUM` changes it.
- `diff` assumes the output device honors tab stops and that ordinary character widths are supplied by the operating system, but these assumptions can be incorrect. [GNU diff manual excerpt](https://manpages.debian.org/testing/diffutils/diff.1.en.html) [development discussion](https://lists.libreplanet.org/archive/html/diffutils-devel/2023-07/txtLnL_3AmLXk.txt)

A 2024 implementation change specifically overhauled column-width and padding calculations and rewrote tab expansion for `--expand-tabs` with `--side-by-side`. [FreeBSD commit summary](https://lists.freebsd.org/archives/dev-commits-src-all/2024-February/038191.html)
